This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 06.12.2023 at about 4.00 to 4.10 p.m. petitioner had been riding motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EP-6430 near Dairy Circle, Bengaluru - SCCH-5 Kanakapura Road, Harohalli Town and Taluk, Ramanagara, at that time, driver of Canter MGV bearing Reg. No.KA-19-AA-6021 has driven the same at very high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner's motor cycle, due to which, he sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to CDSIMER Hospital, Harohalli, after firstaid he was shifted to Supra Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he took treatment as inpatient and he has spent a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical, nourishment and attendant charges.

3. At the time of the accident he was aged about 45 years, hale and healthy, he was doing agricultural work, thereby earning Rs.50,000/- p.m., due to this accident he is not able to attend to his work, resulted in loss of earning and put to great hardship and untold SCCH-5 misery and depressed.
Out of this accident crime No.308/2023 is registered against the driver of the offending Canter before the Harohalli Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is the owner, respondent No.2 is insurer of the said offending vehicle, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has remained absent, hence placed exparte.

Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and submitted that, this respondent is insurer of MGV TATA Goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-19-AA-6021 and liability to indemnify respondent No.1 is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
There is no compliance of SCCH-5 Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further he is entitled to seek protection under Sec.170 of M.V.Act.
Further submitted that, said offending vehicle was not at all involved in the alleged accident and there is lapse of 3 days in lodging the complaint.

Further denied age,
occupation and income of the petitioner.

Further submitted that, driver of the offending vehicle does not possessed valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and petitioner was not wearing prescribed ISI marked helmet and was solely responsible for the alleged c.
Compensation claimed by the petitioner is on higher side.

Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5.

On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, this court has framed the following:

2 SCCH-5 ::ISSUES::
1.
Whether Petitioner proves that, on 06.12.2023 at about 4.00 to 4.10 p.m. when the petitioner was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg.

No.KA-41-EP- 6430 near Diary Circle, Bengaluru - Kanakapura Road, Harohalli Town and Taluk, Ramanagara District, at that point of time, driver of Canter MGV bearing Reg. No.KA-19-AA-6021 driven the same in high speed,m rash and negligent manner dashed against petitioner's motor cycle from behind and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

6. In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW-1, examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. Orthopaedic Surgeon at SOADS as PW-2 and marked 18 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.18 and closed his evidence.

On the other hand, MRO of Chandramma SCCH-5 Dayananda Sagar Hospital is examined as RW-1 and marked documents as per Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.4 and closed evidence.
7.

Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
: : REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as SCCH-5 Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.6.
9 . Further to substantiate the petitioner case, he examined one Doctor as PW-2.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 and records those have marked i.e., FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, IMV Report and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 06.12.2023 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
10.
On the other hand, MRO of Chandramma Dayananda Sagar Hospital is examined as RW-1 and Rajesha vs Sheela Jalan on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144145653/
3 exhibited OPD Book marked as Ex.R.1, copy of police intimation is marked as Ex.R.2, copy of MLC book is marked as Ex.R.3 and authorization letter is marked as SCCH-5 Ex.R.4.
Further except oral evidence, respondent No.2 has not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 06.12.2023 at about 4.00 to 4.10 p.m. when he was riding motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EP-6430 near Diary Circle, Harohalli Town and Taluk, Ramanagara District.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
11. The police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the driver of Canter MGV bearing Reg. No.KA-19-AA-6021.
Under such SCCH-5 circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that,
petitioner
has proved the above issue No.1 in his favour
. Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:-
As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained right clavicle fracture, for the said injuries he was treated with ORIF with plate and screws.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.5, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.7 issued by Supra Hospital,
wherein he took treatment as indoor patient since 07.12.2023 to 09.12.2023.

Further he has furnished outpatient slips marked as Ex.P.8, medical bills to the tune of Rs.1,00,096/- marked as Ex.P.9, sericulture bills marked as Ex.P.10 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.16.
SCCH-5 13.
Further Dr.Nagaraj B.N. Orthopaedic Surgeon at SOADS is examined as PW-2.

To substantiate his evidence, he has exhibited clinical notes marked as Ex.P.17 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.18 and he has assessed total disability of the right arm at 32% and whole body physical disability at 11%.
In cross- examination he has categorically deposed that, he has not treated the petitioner.
Further deposed that, at the time of discharge, the condition of the patient was normal and there is no reference in discharge summary about physiotherapy and now the fracture is united.
Further deposed that, petitioner can do his normal day-to-day activities with some difficulty and petitioner has not sustained any nerve damages.
Further deposed that, he has not assessed the functional disability.

Under such circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries SCCH-5 sustained by the petitioner and also by relying on citation reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s.
Ajay Kumar, the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 11% i.e., 1/3rd to the whole body out of total disability of the right arm at 32%, for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

14. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 45 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.15, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner as 10.05.1978 and the alleged accident is occurred on 06.12.2023, accordingly relying on Ex.P.15 his age is considered about 46 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 13 is applicable as per decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Rajesha vs Sheela Jalan on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144145653/
4 Transport Corporation and others.

As per his case, he was doing agricultural work, thereby earning Rs.50,000/- p.m., to prove the said fact, petitioner has exhibited sericulture bills marked as Ex.P.10, copy of bank statement marked as Ex.P.11, panchayath endorsement marked as Ex.P.12 and RTC's marked as Ex.P.13, but the said documents does not reveal exact income of the petitioner

, that means, merely some of the lands are standing in the name of petitioner and sericulture bills are issued in favour of him have not confirms about definite and permanent income of the petitioner, that too, to treat the said documents for consideration of future loss of income.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at SCCH-5 the rate of Rs.15,250/-
p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is admitted fact that, as per the discharge summary marked as Ex.P.7, petitioner was admitted in Supra Hospital as inpatient from 07.12.2023 to 09.12.2023 i.e., for 2 days.

For the said period he is entitled for the loss of income as per the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner should be taken into consideration i.e., Rs.15,250/- p.m.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the income of said SCCH-5 quantum for the period he was admitted as inpatient in the hospital.

So petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,017/-
towards loss on income during laid up period.
17. Further admittedly petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.9 medical bills for Rs.1,00,096/-.
On perusal of the said bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for this treatment is considered.

Further on perusal of Ex.P.5 in which Doctor who have treated i.e., Dr.Kiran J. has categorically stated that,
petitioner has sustained grievous injury out of the accident caused on 07.12.2023.
So as per Ex.P.5 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained fracture of right clavicle, which is grievous in nature.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Ramesh Babu for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.

So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 and SCCH-5 PW-2 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.
18.
Per contra, except oral evidence, respondents have not taken any endeavors to prove the allegations as alleged in the written statement.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, merely respondents have filed written statement and they have denied entire case of the petitioner are all not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case, because it is bounden duty of them to prove the defence as taken in the written statement.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for medical bills and other compensation as stated below.

Further during the course of the argument, respondent No.2 counsel Sri.JS argued that,
petitioner has not examined the treated Doctor and PW-1 is SCCH-5 45 years old, no agriculture income has proved etc., the said arguments are considered for an aforesaid extent.

20. Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-
Sl
. No .
Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of Future Income 2,61,690-00 2.
Pain and sufferings 15,000-00 3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,000-00 attendant charges
4. Medical Expenses 1,00,096-00 5. Loss of amenities in life 15,000-00 6.
Loss of income during laid up 1,017-00 period Total 4,07,803-00 21.
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,07,803/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.
SCCH-5 22.

In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.422208/31/2024/4902 which is valid for the period from 05.09.2023 to 04.09.2024, the alleged accident was occurred on 06.12.2023 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.
Hence respondent No.2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.

23. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,07,803/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Seven SCCH-5 Thousand Eight Hundred Three Only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

6
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
